question.text: This man had formerly served as the Collector of the Port of New York before being fired. This successor of James Garfield as president signed the Pendleton Civil Service Act into law.
question.clue: He restructured much of Buchanan's Morrill Tariff with a tariff act labeled the "Mongrel," and accepted a spot on his ticket after the refusal of Levi Morton.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the landmark interstate commerce case Gibbons v. Ogden.
swap.text: This American entrepreneur, nicknamed "Commodore," worked as a steamboat captain and business manager for Gibbons, and combatted other steamboat monopolies before building a railroad empire.
swap.clue: This man served as a business manager for Thomas Gibbons before clashing with Daniel Drew over use of the Hudson River.

question.text: Bryan lost the 1896 Presidential election after being heavily outspent by this man. He was succeeded by Theodore Roosevelt after his 1901 assassination in Buffalo, New York.
question.clue: This president won an election in which the "Cross of Gold" speech was given by William Jennings Bryan.

swap.text: After working with steamboats, Vanderbilt rose to the top of the industry making networks of these tracks across the nation. A major event in that industry's history was the construction of a Transcontinental one.
swap.clue: Jay Gould and James Fisk struggled for control in the Erie War against the most powerful executive in this industry, Cornelius Vanderbilt.

question.text: This Carnegie steel manager was primarily responsible for handling the Pinkertons. Almost assassinated by Alexander Berkman, this man also owned a whiskey company with Andrew Mellon.
question.clue: Joseph Duveen advised this man on purchasing works like Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl for his Fifth Avenue mansion.

swap.leadin: The military built Fort Gibson here in 1795. -.
swap.text: Name this island that processed 12 million newcomers when it housed an immigration station. This island is about a mile north of the Statue of Liberty.
swap.clue: Halifax's Pier 21 was the Canadian analogue of this successor of Castle Garden, where Lewis Hine photographed people with luggage in Climbing into the Promised Land.

question.text: After being imprisoned for his drag balls, Swann petitioned this President for a pardon. After he had an illegitimate child with Maria Halpin, this President was targeted with the chant "Ma, Ma, where's my Pa."
question.clue: Despite a severe drought, this man famously vetoed the Texas Seed Bill, which saw him earn the nickname "His Obstinacy."

swap.leadin: This presidential election saw two separate Prohibition Party candidates run for office, and it led to the Gold Standard Act.
swap.text: Name this election for which Free Silver advocate William Jennings Bryan gave his "Cross of Gold" speech at the Democratic National Convention. Bryan eventually wound up forty-eight electoral votes short of the presidency.
swap.clue: Thomas Watson repudiated the vice presidential candidacy of Arthur Sewall in this election.

question.leadin: Name these political organizations of New York.
question.text: William Mooney founded this group, which originally utilized elaborate Indian rituals. Its notable leaders included Fernando Wood and Boss Tweed.
question.clue: One of its final leaders was Carmine DeSapio, and this group also distinguished between "honest" and "dishonest" graft after being led by William Plunkitt.

swap.text: In response to a company owner's wage cuts, Eugene Debs called for this 1894 strike, where railway workers refused to service cars by that company.
swap.clue: Mediation offers by the local Civic Federation and Mayor John P. Hopkins were turned down, and violence soon broke out at Blue Island.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the free silver debate in American politics.
question.text: This politician's namesake Silver Purchase Act of 1890 replaced the similar Bland-Allison Act and increased the amount of silver the government was required to purchase each month. This man also named a law strengthened by a 1914 law named for Henry Clayton Jr.
question.clue: This politician drafted, and later carried out, the 1875 Resumption Act, which restored the gold standard.

swap.leadin: Identify the following people connected with a certain strike.
swap.text: The strike got ugly when the National Guard was called out under this general, who would later distinguish himself by leading the invasion of Puerto Rico in the Spanish-American War and capturing Geronimo.
swap.clue: His other notable success was shared with Oliver Otis Howard and saw its climax at Bear Paw ravine.

question.text: Chicago businessman Montgomery Ward, a competitor of this man, financed early Grange consumer cooperatives in the 1870s. After retiring, this man left his mail-order business to Julius Rosenwald.

swap.leadin: John Keegan called this man "the most important American strategist of the nineteenth century."
swap.text: Name this man who extolled the importance of sea power in warfare. His ideas inspired the Anglo-German naval arms race before World War I.
swap.clue: Citing this theorist, Alfred von Tirpitz acquired support for the construction of a large surface fleet from Wilhelm II.

question.text: The Battle of White Bird Canyon began this 1877 conflict after the US sought to take ninety percent of a reservation for its gold. The "Steal Treaty" that sparked this conflict established the Lapwai Reservation.

swap.text: This group of demands presented in 1890 demanded the free circulation of silver and the abolition of national banks. It is named for the Florida city in which it was given.
swap.clue: The meeting that produced this document took place at the Marion Opera House, and this document takes the form of seven numbered resolutions.

question.leadin: Answer the following about legal battles over polygamy in the Utah Territory.
question.text: This 1874 statute, named for a Senator from Vermont, redefined the judiciary system in the Utah Territory as being under the federal district courts, which ended the dominance of church officials. It was followed by the Edmunds Act, making polygamy a felony.

swap.leadin: Tyler Anbinder notes how the description of this person by New York Times as "a little rosy-cheeked Irish girl" selectively ignored her fellow passengers primarily from Eastern and Southern Europe.
swap.text: Name this teen who, on New Year's Day, 1892, became the first registered immigrant at Ellis Island.

question.text: Leacock is sometimes considered the Canadian equivalent of this American author of Roughing It and The Innocents Abroad.
question.clue: In "To My Missionary Critics," this man savaged Reverend William Scott Ament for collecting Boxer indemnities from Chinese villagers. He also criticized missionaries in an essay blasting "the Blessings-of-Civilization Trust."

swap.leadin: He dropped out of consideration for the democratic ticket in the election of 1900 after claiming the president's job was simply following orders from congress.
swap.text: Name this man who was the sole Admiral of the Navy and led the American fleet at the Battle of Manilla Bay.
swap.clue: This man annihilated the fleet of Patricio Montojo y Pasaron by issuing the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley" while on board his flagship, the USS Olympia.
